groups.notes: Nine eligible units, all integrated, all started at ladder index 0 - the only step this repository has ever measured. Recommendation retained unchanged. Group confidence is low despite n=9 because the sample is single-armed: costToAcceptance can rank units against each other but cannot rank steps against each other, which is what a start recommendation requires. Three of nine were accepted on the first review with no fix pass; six required at least one fix pass and re-review. That re-review rate is a hint that a stronger start might be cheaper, but the rubric's floor-raise grounds are not met: no capability failure was recorded on any unit, and no stronger step was ever run, so the required 25%-lower-median comparison cannot be computed. No floor lowering is possible either - index 0 is the lowest verified step - and for the same reason no boundary probe is schedulable below it. CONFOUND, stated explicitly rather than controlled: costToAcceptance here is driven jointly by attempt count and by context size, and the two are not separable in this telemetry. Issue #50 (large group) is the clearest illustration - accepted on the first review with zero findings and still the second most expensive unit in the run at $17.75 - and the same effect is present inside this group (#59 cost $24.32 across 3 attempts on a 1235-line single-file change, while #49 cost $7.30 across 3 attempts on a 187-line change). Any future ranking of steps by median costToAcceptance in this group must normalise for change size or it will attribute context cost to route quality. capabilityEscalation is recorded as 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary.

groups.notes: Three eligible units, all integrated at ladder index 0. Recommendation retained unchanged; three units cannot carry a per-size threshold and, as with the other groups, no stronger step was ever run so no comparison is available. #50 and #57 were accepted on their first review with no fix pass (#57's second session is a merger, not a fix pass); #58 required one fix pass. CONFOUND: this group is where the cost/context confound is most visible. #50 is the second most expensive unit in the entire run at $17.75 despite one attempt and one clean review, purely because its context was large - a grouping that reads costToAcceptance as a proxy for route quality would rank #50's step as poor when the step in fact landed it first time. The median recorded here ($13.09) should therefore not be compared against another group's median or against a future step's median without normalising for change size. capabilityEscalation is recorded as 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary.

findings.detail: Generally available; $5/MTok in, $25/MTok out; 1M context. Occupies the upper half of the verified ladder and has never been run as an implementer in this repository, so it can only enter the candidate order on external evidence.

Introductory pricing lapses 2026-08-31. This silently re-prices every ladder step this repository has ever measured by +50% per token with no change to the route itself. Recorded with effectiveAt so the next run treats it as already-known rather than as news.

No cost-per-completed-task or tokens-per-task benchmark could be cited for either candidate route. relativeTokensForComparableWork is left null in every externalPrior; per-token price alone must not be used to rank these steps.

implications: All measured costToAcceptance figures in this file were incurred at claude-sonnet-5 introductory pricing and are not directly comparable to observations recorded after 2026-09-01.

The +50% applies to the whole ladder bottom, so it narrows the price gap to claude-opus-5 without providing any evidence about its quality. It is a reason to re-run the comparison, not a reason to change the floor.
